title: CERTIFIED VS. EMPIRICAL ADVERSARIAL ROBUSTNESS VIA HYBRID CONVOLUTIONS WITH ATTENTION STOCHASTICITY
claim: A parallel multi-stream architecture with gated fusion and residual noise injection composes into one network with a bounded Lipschitz constant.
layout: Single panel, left-to-right, three parallel branches merging via gated sum
description: A single wide diagram with an orange border, read left to right. An ImageNet panda photo labeled 'Input x' fans out into three horizontal branches. The top branch is a pink FDPAN box, the middle is a light-purple SNCAN box, and the bottom is a Jacobian Orthogonal box (orange) followed by a green RPFAN box. Each branch is tagged '2-Lipschitz' and has a formula label such as G_FDPAN(x; ξ, M_ω). Each branch outputs a noisy green-gray feature-map grid. Each grid is multiplied by a gate α_{b,c} at a ⊗ node. The three results meet at a ⊕ node and form the fused G_b(·;Ω) grid. That grid passes through a pink RANI block (1-Lipschitz) with a skip connection (2-Lipschitz) into a second ⊕ node, giving the output z. The eye goes first to the colored boxes and the feature grids.
caption: Overview of HyCAS mechanism. It consists of three parallel streams—FDPAN, SNCAN, and RPFAN—each built from 1-Lipschitz cores with Randomized Attention Noise Injection (RANI) residuals. Per-channel convex gating fuses the streams to form Gb(; Ω). Each stream is ≤ 2-Lipschitz; the fused stream and the stacked network remain ≤ 2-Lipschitz, enabling a margin-based ℓ2 certificate.
abstract: We introduce Hybrid Convolutions with Attention Stochasticity (HyCAS), an adversarial defense that narrows the long-standing gap between provable robustness under L2 certificates and empirical robustness against strong L attacks, while preserving strong generalization across diverse imaging benchmarks. HyCAS unifies deterministic and randomized principles by coupling 1-Lipschitz, spectrally normalized convolutions with two stochastic components, spectral normalized random, projection filters and a randomized attention-noise mechanism, to realize a randomized defense. Injecting smoothing randomness inside the architecture yields an overall <= 2-Lipschitz network with formal certificates. Exten-sive experiments on diverse imaging benchmarks, including CIFAR-10/100, ImageNet-1k, NIH Chest X-ray, HAM10000, show that HyCAS surpasses prior leading certified and empirical defenses, boosting certified accuracy by up to 7.3% (on NIH Chest X-ray) and empirical robustness by up to 3.1% (on HAM10000), without sacrificing clean accuracy. These results show that a randomized Lipschitz constrained architecture can simultaneously improve both certified L2 and empirical L adversarial robustness, thereby supporting safer deployment of deep models in high-stakes applications. Code: https://github.com/misti1203/HyCAS
